build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Each floor is a procedurally generated platformer level with an exit at the bottom. The layout changes every run — platforms, traps, and enemy placement are randomized. Score 0 if levels are static.

The explorer has limited tools: ropes (create climbable lines upward) and bombs (destroy terrain). Both are consumable and scarce. Using them is a meaningful resource decision. Score 0 if no consumable tools exist.

Physics objects (pots, crates, skulls) can be picked up and thrown at enemies or traps. Objects interact with the environment — thrown pots trigger arrow traps, crates break on impact. Score 0 if no throwable objects exist.

A ghost timer activates after lingering too long on a floor (approximately 3 minutes), spawning an invincible pursuer that forces the player to move forward. The ghost is visible and threatening. Score 0 if no time pressure exists.

Death is permanent — dying sends the player back to floor 1 with no carried resources. Health persists across floors within a run. The run ends on a game-over screen with stats. Score 0 if death has no consequence or health resets between floors.

At least 4 distinct trap types exist (arrow traps, spike pits, crush blocks, dart blowers) each with different trigger conditions and avoidance strategies. Traps interact with physics objects. Score 0 if no traps exist.

Shops appear every few floors with items for sale (health, tools, weapons, accessories). A shopkeeper NPC is present. Stealing triggers shopkeeper aggression for the rest of the run. Score 0 if no shops exist.

At least 3 distinct environment themes change every few floors (caves, jungle, ice, temple) with different enemy types, trap configurations, and visual styles per theme. Score 0 if the environment never changes.

At least 5 distinct enemy types with different behaviors (patrollers, jumpers, flyers, spitters, exploders). Enemies interact with traps and physics objects. Score 0 if fewer than 3 enemy types exist.

A game-over screen shows depth reached, gold collected, enemies defeated, and cause of death. A shortcut system unlocks after meeting conditions, allowing experienced players to start at later floors. Score 0 if no results or shortcuts exist.
A styled title screen shows the cave entrance with depth markers and the game name. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> descent -> floors -> shops -> game over -> retry without restarting. The ghost timer and floor transitions are smooth. Score 0 if transitions are missing.
During gameplay, health, gold, rope count, bomb count, and current floor are visible in a clear HUD. The ghost timer warning is visible when approaching the limit. Score 0 if no HUD exists.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: the explorer, enemies, traps, physics objects, terrain, and collectibles are all clearly distinguishable. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, floors, enemies, traps, shops, and UI — a consistent spelunking adventure aesthetic with earthy palette. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Cave environments use real sprite or tile art for terrain, traps, enemies, and the explorer — not plain ColorRect fills. Different themes have distinct tilesets. Score 0 if environments are uniform color fills.

HUD and UI chrome: health display, item counters, shop interface, and game-over screen use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: the explorer has run/jump/whip animations, enemies have movement animations, traps trigger with visible wind-up, bombs explode with particles, and the ghost has a menacing entrance animation. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
